## 3 Chamber Sociability Test

-- **Duration - 3 times 10 minutes [habituation, social preference, social recognition]**   
Spontaneous social interaction can be rapidly and objectively assessed in the ‘sociability test’ followed by the ‘preference for social novelty test’ in the tripartite chamber. These two tasks take advantage of the spontaneous interest of a normal mouse for another unfamiliar mouse. These tests can be used to model symptoms of human disorders associated with social approach abnormalities such as autism, William’s syndrome, social phobias and schizophrenia (Yang et al., 2011; Moy et al., 2004).  

- *Moy SS, Nadler JJ, Perez A, Barbaro RP, Johns JM, Magnuson TR, Piven J, Crawley JN. Sociability and preference for social novelty in five inbred strains: an approach to assess autistic-like behavior in mice. Genes Brain Behav. 2004 Oct;3(5):287-302. doi: 10.1111/j.1601-1848.2004.00076.x. PMID: 15344922*  

- *Yang, M., Silverman, J. L. & Crawley, J. N. Automated three-chambered social approach task for mice. Curr. Protoc. Neurosci. Chapter 8, Unit 8.26 (2011).*   

-- **Parameters\:**   
Primary variable of interest: time spent in each chamber (habituation and both tests), time spent at each grid (during both tests: at stranger 1, stranger 2 and empty), Discrimination ratio [Discrimination Ratio = (Time spent at Novel animal (Stranger2) [TN] - Time spent at Familiar animal (Stranger 1) [TF])/(TN + TF)].  
Secondary variables: number of visits to each chamber, latency to each chamber, track length. 


-- **Illustration:**  
Boxplots and individual scores  

```{r data_loading_3ch}

#here we clear the working directory again in case the script is used as a child
rm(list = ls())
#save the path to the working direcotry into the variable dir
dir = getwd()

#--------------------------- 1. Manual Entries -----------------------------#
# Please enter here the following variables:

# 1.1 INPUT FILES 
#IMPORTANT: Please also check the renaming of the columns in 'LOAD DATA' !!!!!!
file_path <- "~/6. Data from Behavioral Tests/analysis/3 chamber test/"

file_path_MR <- "~/6. Data from Behavioral Tests/analysis/3 chamber test/"

raw_data_file <- "2001_Rosario_A46_3 chamber test_data_Cohort 1_2022-11-11.csv"

lookup_path <- "~/6. Data from Behavioral Tests/"
lookup_path_MR <- "~/6. Data from Behavioral Tests/"
 
lookup_file_c1 <- "Rosario_A46_Real_lookup.xlsx"

# 1.3 PLOT
#here we define the colors we going to use for the different strains in the plots
color_strain <- c("#0099CC", "#FF9900") 

color_flu <- c('#0099CC', '#FF9900', '#DC143C', '#8B008B')
# colors for Geiger project that has 4 treatment strains

color_control <- c('#8B008B', '#0000FF', '#008000')
# colors for control data for all 5 projects

#---------------------------LOAD DATA-----------------------------#
# Load data
#evaluate read_excel function with given filepath
raw_data <- read_delim(paste(file_path,raw_data_file, sep=""), delim=",") 
  
# Load lookup file with ID, cohort and genotype infos
#evaluate read_excel function with given filepath
lookup <- tryCatch(read_excel(paste(lookup_path,lookup_file_c1, sep="")), # Process any error messages and try another filepath
                   error= function(e) {
  #print a small message with both filepaths
  print(paste0('filepath: ', lookup_path, ' not found! Trying ', lookup_path_MR, ' instead.'))
  lookup <- read_excel(paste(lookup_path_MR,lookup_file_c1, sep=""))
})

# Generate colors for individual animals (with lookup file)
IDcolor <- tibble(IDcolor=distinctColorPalette(length(lookup$ID)))

#create a dataframe with with cohort, ID and IDcolor 
lookup_color <- lookup %>%
  dplyr::select(cohort,ID) %>%
#  dplyr::select(cohort,ID, "S1/side", "S2/side") %>%
  bind_cols(IDcolor)

#get list of strains without NAs
list_of_genotypes <- sort(na.omit(unique(raw_data$genotype)), decreasing = T)

# Combine the lookup file
data <- raw_data %>%
  merge(lookup_color, by = c("cohort", "ID"), all = TRUE)%>%
  rename( 
    Dur_l  = `Duration_(s)_left_side`,
    Dur_c  = `Duration_(s)_center`,
    Dur_r  = `Duration_(s)_right_side`,
    Dur_e  = `Duration_(s)_Empty`,
    Dur_s1 = `Duration_(s)_St1`,
    Dur_s2 = `Duration_(s)_St2`,
    
    TL_l  = `Tracklength_(cm)_left_side`,
    TL_c  = `Tracklength_(cm)_center`,
    TL_r  = `Tracklength_(cm)_right_side`,
    TL_e  = `Tracklength_(cm)_Empty`,
    TL_s1 = `Tracklength_(cm)_St1`,
    TL_s2 = `Tracklength_(cm)_St2`
  )%>%
  mutate(Genotype = factor(genotype, levels = list_of_genotypes), 
         Cohort = as.factor(cohort))

# 1.2 EXPERIMENTAL SETTINGS
#how many cohorts?
list_of_cohorts <- unique(data$cohort)
number_of_cohorts <- length(list_of_cohorts)

genotype1= paste('n_mice', list_of_genotypes[1], sep='_')
genotype2 = paste('n_mice', list_of_genotypes[2], sep='_')

cohort_data <- data.frame('cohort'=numeric(0),
                          'n_mice_total' = numeric(0), 
                          genotype1 = numeric(0),
                          genotype2 = numeric(0),
                          'timepoint'= numeric(0))

for(c in list_of_cohorts) {
  data_cohort <- data %>%
    filter(cohort == c,
           phase== "hab",
           no == "Sum")
  
  n_mice_total = nrow(data_cohort)
  timepoint = 1
  n_genotypes <- c()
  for(st in list_of_genotypes){
    data_cohort_genotype <- data_cohort %>%
      filter(Genotype == st)
    n_genotype = nrow(data_cohort_genotype)
  
  n_genotypes <- c(n_genotypes, n_genotype)
  }
  cohort_vec <- c(c, n_mice_total, n_genotypes, timepoint)
  
  cohort_data <- rbind(cohort_data, cohort_vec) 
  
}
colnames(cohort_data) <- c("cohort", "n_total", "n_genotype1", "n_genotype2", "timepoint")


#>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>

# UPDATE:
# phases == Test types
# phases are hab, S1, S2
#
# Notes

# Test types are: hab = habituation, 
# soc = sociability (introduction of stranger 1), 
# nov = social novelty (introduction of stranger 2 in presence of stranger 1)
#>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>

# Column name explanations:

# No.: The interval number is assigned in chronological order
# Date: Actual date of the end time of the interval in the format day.month.year
# Time: Time of the day when the interval ended.
# Avg. velocity (cm/s): Average speed, measured in the whole arena 
# Track length (cm): Total length of the track, measured in the whole arena
# Activity (%): Amount of time in which the animal's movement speed exceeded the Activity threshold
# (user defined on the Configuration − Activity tab)
# Ambulations: Total count of accelerations from zero to a speed, defined as Ambulation threshold
# (user defined on the Configuration − Activity tab)
# ZC: Total count of Zone crossings (user defined on the Configuration − Activity tab)
# RZC: Total count of Rated zone crossings (user defined on the Configuration − Activity tab)
# Wall dist. (cm): Distance of the animal's body point to the nearest wall, averaged over all video frames
# (the wall is user defined on the Configuration − Activity tab) NOT USED FOR THIS TEST!
# For Velocity classes:
# vc1 to vc10: Time the animal spent moving with a speed according to a Velocity class
# (user defined on the Configuration − Activity tab) NOT USED FOR THIS TEST!
# For each zone:
# Duration (s): of stay Total time the animal's reference point (user defined on the Configuration − Zone
# definition tab) stayed in a zone
# Velocity (cm/s): Average speed, measured during the Duration of stay
# Track length (cm): Total length of the track, measured in during the Duration of stay
# Visits Total count of zone entries by the reference point
# Headbobs: Total count of the specific behavior (user defined on the Configuration − Behavior
# tab) during the Duration of stay NOT USED FOR THIS TEST!
# Tailmoves: Total count of the specific behavior (user defined on the Configuration − Behavior
# tab) during the Duration of stay NOT USED FOR THIS TEST!
# Headstretches: Total count of the specific behavior (user defined on the Configuration − Behavior
# tab) during the Duration of stay NOT USED FOR THIS TEST!
# Freezings: Total count of the specific behavior (user defined on the Configuration − Behavior
# tab) during the Duration of stay NOT USED FOR THIS TEST!
# Activity (%): Amount of active time in the zone during the Duration of interval
# Ambulations: Total count of Ambulations in the zone during Duration of interval
# Visit latency: Elapsed time to the zone entry since the saving interval started
# 
# --The classical parameter is a 
# Discrimination Ratio= (Time spent at Novel animal (Stranger2) [TN] - Time spent at Familiar animal (Stranger 1) [TF])/(TN + TF);
# but other parameters such as 
# Exploration time: %T= (TN or TF/(TN +TF)) x100 and 
# Frequency of visits: total number of visit to the other animals , can also be interesting to evaluate. 
# These parameters can be calculated for the sociability phase and preference for social novelty phase. 
# The parameter "Track length” was extracted in order to control for locomotion bias in this motoric task
# 
# The parameters assessed manually are number of sniffs at wire cages, the number of feces and the number of urine.    
```

### Experimental conditions

1 cohort of mice:  
* Cohort 1: $n$ = `r cohort_data$n_total[1]` (`r cohort_data$n_genotype1[1]` `r list_of_genotypes[1]` + `r cohort_data$n_genotype2[1]` `r list_of_genotypes[2]`)  
   
Time point: `r cohort_data$timepoint[1]`  
Genotype: `r list_of_genotypes`   
Experimenter:    

```{r data_dur_inter_3ch}
# Prepare the data for duration of interaction analysis

#--------------------------DURATION OF INTERACTION----------------------------#

# SOCIAL PREFERENCE DATA-------------------------------------------

# Method 1, where the duration is the time spent in the st1 or st2 zones,
# which are different than the left and right areas.
# Social preference: st1 zone - unfamiliar, st2 zone - empty
# Social recognition: st1 zone - familiar, st2 zone - unfamiliar

# Extract the social preference test data by filtering "soc"
# rename st1_dur as unfamiliar
# rename st2_dur as empty


soc_dur <- data %>%
  filter(phase == "soc") %>%
  #add 2 columns empty and unfamiliar, which are copies of the columns Dur_e and Dur_s1 
  mutate(empty = Dur_e, unfamiliar = Dur_s1) %>%
  #dplyr::select(no, cohort, ID, phase, strain, empty, unfamiliar, IDcolor, Strain, Cohort) %>%
  #convert this columns to long-format
  gather(grid, dur, empty, unfamiliar)
# Exclude animals
# exclude animals with NA values for duration in either empty or unfamiliar zones
excluded_animals_socdur <- soc_dur[is.na(soc_dur$dur) | is.na(soc_dur$Genotype),] %>%
  filter(no=="Sum") %>%
  group_by(cohort, phase, Genotype, ID)
# update data --> this data will only be used for analysis of this parameter
soc_dur <- soc_dur[!is.na(soc_dur$dur) & !is.na(soc_dur$Genotype),] #this only excludes the NAs, but not all data of animals with NAs


# Method 2
# Choose duration in the left or right area based on where the st1 was placed
# this is different than the soc_dur, where the duration for each zone
# ST1 or ST2 was selected
soc_dur2 <- data %>%
  filter(phase == "soc") #%>%
  #dplyr::select(no, cohort, ID, phase, strain, Dur_l, Dur_r, IDcolor, side_st1, Strain)
# Exclude animals
# exclude animals with NA values for st1_side info and with NA values in left or right areas
excluded_animals_socdur2 <- soc_dur2[is.na(soc_dur2$side_st1) | is.na(soc_dur2$Dur_l) | is.na(soc_dur2$Dur_r) | is.na(soc_dur2$Genotype),] %>%
  filter(no=="Sum") %>%
  group_by( cohort, phase, Genotype, ID)
# update data --> this data will only be used for analysis of this parameter
soc_dur2 <- soc_dur2[!is.na(soc_dur2$side_st1) & !is.na(soc_dur2$Dur_l) & !is.na(soc_dur2$Dur_r) & !is.na(soc_dur2$Genotype),] 

# Select duration values based on which side the st1 was placed:
# if st1 was placed on the right side 'r', then the duration of unfamiliar is r_dur and duration of empty is l_dur
# and vice versa
for (i in 1:nrow(soc_dur2)) {
  if (soc_dur2$side_st1[i] == "r") {
    soc_dur2$unfamiliar[i] = soc_dur2$Dur_r[i]
    soc_dur2$empty[i] = soc_dur2$Dur_l[i]}
  if (soc_dur2$side_st1[i] == "l") {
   soc_dur2$unfamiliar[i] = soc_dur2$Dur_l[i]
   soc_dur2$empty[i] = soc_dur2$Dur_r[i]}
}
#convert to long format
soc_dur2 <- soc_dur2 %>%
  gather(grid, dur, unfamiliar, empty)


# SOCIAL RECOGNITION DATA -------------------------------------------

# Method 1, where the duration is the time spent in the st1 or st2 zones,
# which are different than the left and right areas.
# Social preference: st1 zone - unfamiliar, st2 zone - empty
# Social recognition: st1 zone - familiar, st2 zone - unfamiliar

# Extract the social recognition test data by filtering "rec"
# rename st1_dur as familiar
# rename st2_dur as unfamiliar
rec_dur <- data %>%
  filter(phase == "nov") %>%
  mutate(familiar = Dur_s1, unfamiliar = Dur_s2) %>%
  #dplyr::select(no, cohort, ID, phase, strain, familiar, unfamiliar, IDcolor, Strain) %>%
  gather(grid, dur, familiar, unfamiliar)
# Exclude animals
# exclude animals with NA values for duration in either empty or unfamiliar zones
excluded_animals_recdur <- rec_dur[is.na(rec_dur$dur) | is.na(rec_dur$Genotype),] %>%
  filter(no=="Sum") %>%
  group_by(cohort, phase, Genotype, ID)
# update data --> this data will only be used for analysis of this parameter
rec_dur <- rec_dur[!is.na(rec_dur$dur) & !is.na(rec_dur$Genotype),]


# Method 2
# Choose duration in the left or right area based on where the st1 was placed
# this is different than the soc_dur, where the duration for each zone
# ST1 or ST2 was selected
rec_dur2 <- data %>%
  filter(phase == "nov") #%>%
  #dplyr::select(no, cohort, ID, phase, strain, Dur_l,Dur_r, IDcolor, side_st1, Strain)
# Exclude animals
# exclude animals with NA values for st1_side info and with NA values in left or right areas
excluded_animals_recdur2 <- rec_dur2[is.na(rec_dur2$side_st1) | is.na(rec_dur2$Dur_l) | is.na(rec_dur2$Dur_r) | is.na(rec_dur2$Genotype),] %>%
  filter(no=="Sum") %>%
  group_by(cohort, phase, Genotype, ID)
# update data --> this data will only be used for analysis of this parameter
rec_dur2 <- rec_dur2[!is.na(rec_dur2$side_st1) & !is.na(rec_dur2$Dur_l) & !is.na(rec_dur2$Dur_r) & !is.na(rec_dur2$Genotype),] 

# Select duration values based on which side the st1 was placed:
# if st1 was placed on the right side 'r', then the duration of familiar is r_dur and unfamilair is l_dur
# and vice versa
for (i in 1:nrow(rec_dur2)) {
  if (rec_dur2$side_st1[i] == "r") {
    rec_dur2$familiar[i] = rec_dur2$Dur_r[i]
    rec_dur2$unfamiliar[i] = rec_dur2$Dur_l[i]}
  if (rec_dur2$side_st1[i] == "l") {
   rec_dur2$familiar[i] = rec_dur2$Dur_l[i]
   rec_dur2$unfamiliar [i] = rec_dur2$Dur_r[i]}
}
#convert to long format
rec_dur2 <- rec_dur2 %>%
  gather(grid, dur, unfamiliar, familiar)

```



```{r data_DR}
# Prepare the data for discrimination ratio analysis 

#--------------------------10MIN DISCRIMINATION RATIO----------------------------#

# SOCIAL PREFERENCE DATA ---------------------------------------------

# Method 1, where the duration is the time spent in the st1 or st2 zones,
# which are different than the left and right areas.
# Social preference: st1 zone - unfamiliar, st2 zone - empty
# Social recognition: st1 zone - familiar, st2 zone - unfamiliar

# Extract the social recognition test data by filtering "rec"
soc_DR <- data %>%
  filter(phase == "soc")# %>%
  #dplyr::select(no, cohort, ID, phase, strain, Dur_s1, Dur_e, IDcolor, Strain)
# Exclude animals
# exclude animals with NA values for duration in either empty or unfamiliar zones
excluded_animals_socDR <- soc_DR[is.na(soc_DR$Dur_e) | is.na(soc_DR$Dur_e) | is.na(soc_DR$Genotype),] %>%
  filter(no=="Sum") %>%
  group_by(cohort, phase, Genotype, ID)
# update data --> this data will only be used for analysis of this parameter
soc_DR <- soc_DR[!is.na(soc_DR$Dur_s1) & !is.na(soc_DR$Dur_e) & !is.na(soc_DR$Genotype),] 

# Calculate DR 
for (i in 1:nrow(soc_DR)) {
  soc_DR$DR[i] = (soc_DR$Dur_s1[i] - soc_DR$Dur_e[i])/(soc_DR$Dur_s1[i] + soc_DR$Dur_e[i])
}

# Method 2
# Choose duration in the left or right area based on where the st1 was placed
# this is different than the soc_dur, where the duration for each zone
# ST1 or ST2 was selected# SOCIAL PREFERENCE DATA

# Extract the social preference test data by filtering "soc"
# rename st1_dur as unfamiliar
# rename st2_dur as empty
soc_DR2 <- data %>%
  filter(phase == "soc") #%>%
  #dplyr::select(no, cohort, ID, phase, strain, Dur_l, Dur_r, IDcolor, side_st1, Strain)
# Exclude animals
# exclude animals with NA values for st1_side info and with NA values in left or right areas
excluded_animals_socDR2 <- soc_DR2[is.na(soc_DR2$side_st1) | is.na(soc_DR2$Dur_l) | is.na(soc_DR2$Dur_r) | is.na(soc_DR2$Genotype),] %>%
  filter(no=="Sum") %>%
  group_by(cohort, phase, Genotype, ID)
# update data --> this data will only be used for analysis of this parameter
soc_DR2 <- soc_DR2[!is.na(soc_DR2$side_st1) & !is.na(soc_DR2$Dur_l) & !is.na(soc_DR2$Dur_r) & !is.na(soc_DR2$Genotype),]

# Calculate DR values based on which side the st1 was placed:
# if st1 was placed on the right side 'r', then the DR is (r_dur - l_dur)/sum
# and vice versa
for (i in 1:nrow(soc_DR2)) {
  if (soc_DR2$side_st1[i] == "r") {
    soc_DR2$DR[i] = (soc_DR2$Dur_r[i] - soc_DR2$Dur_l[i])/(soc_DR2$Dur_r[i] + soc_DR2$Dur_l[i])}
  if (soc_DR2$side_st1[i] == "l") {
    soc_DR2$DR[i] = (soc_DR2$Dur_l[i] - soc_DR2$Dur_r[i])/(soc_DR2$Dur_r[i] + soc_DR2$Dur_l[i])}
}
  

# SOCIAL RECOGNITION DATA ---------------------------------------------

# Method 1, where the duration is the time spent in the st1 or st2 zones,
# which are different than the left and right areas.
# Social preference: st1 zone - unfamiliar, st2 zone - empty
# Social recognition: st1 zone - familiar, st2 zone - unfamiliar

# Extract the social recognition test data by filtering "rec"
rec_DR <- data %>%
  filter(phase == "nov") #%>%
  #dplyr::select(no, cohort, ID, phase, strain, Dur_s1, Dur_s2, IDcolor, Strain)
# Exclude animals
# exclude animals with NA values for duration in either empty or unfamiliar zones
excluded_animals_recDR <- rec_DR[is.na(rec_DR$Dur_s1) | is.na(rec_DR$Dur_s2) | is.na(rec_DR$Genotype),] %>%
  filter(no=="Sum") %>%
  group_by(cohort, phase, Genotype, ID)
# update data --> this data will only be used for analysis of this parameter
rec_DR <- rec_DR[!is.na(rec_DR$Dur_s1) & !is.na(rec_DR$Dur_s2) & !is.na(rec_DR$Genotype),] 

# Calculate DR 
for (i in 1:nrow(rec_DR)) {
  rec_DR$DR[i] = (rec_DR$Dur_s2[i] - rec_DR$Dur_s1[i])/(rec_DR$Dur_s1[i] + rec_DR$Dur_s2[i])
}


# Method 2
# Choose duration in the left or right area based on where the st1 was placed
# this is different than the soc_dur, where the duration for each zone
# ST1 or ST2 was selected

# Extract the social recognition test data by filtering "rec"
# rename st1_dur as familiar
# rename st2_dur as unfamiliar
rec_DR2 <- data %>%
  filter(phase == "nov") #%>%
  #dplyr::select(no, cohort, ID, phase, strain, Dur_l, Dur_r, IDcolor, side_st1, Strain)
# Exclude animals
# exclude animals with NA values for st1_side info and with NA values in left or right areas
excluded_animals_recDR2 <- rec_DR2[is.na(rec_DR2$side_st1) | is.na(rec_DR2$Dur_l) | is.na(rec_DR2$Dur_r) | is.na(rec_DR2$Genotype),] %>%
  filter(no=="Sum") %>%
  group_by(cohort, phase, Genotype, ID)
# update data --> this data will only be used for analysis of this parameter
rec_DR2 <- rec_DR2[!is.na(rec_DR2$side_st1) & !is.na(rec_DR2$Dur_l) & !is.na(rec_DR2$Dur_r) & !is.na(rec_DR2$Genotype),]

# Calculate DR values based on which side the st1 was placed:
# if st1 was placed on the right side 'r', then the DR is (l_dur - r_dur)/sum
# and vice versa
for (i in 1:nrow(rec_DR2)) {
  if (rec_DR2$side_st1[i] == "r") {
    rec_DR2$DR[i] = (rec_DR2$Dur_l[i] - rec_DR2$Dur_r[i])/(rec_DR2$Dur_r[i] + rec_DR2$Dur_l[i])}
  if (rec_DR2$side_st1[i] == "l") {
    rec_DR2$DR[i] = (rec_DR2$Dur_r[i] - rec_DR2$Dur_l[i])/(rec_DR2$Dur_r[i] + rec_DR2$Dur_l[i])}
}


#--------------------------5MIN BINNED DISCRIMINATION RATIO----------------------------#

# Method 2

soc_DR2_5min <- soc_DR2 %>%
  filter(no!="Sum") %>%
  mutate(bin = case_when(
    no %in% 1:5 ~ "1-5 min",
    no %in% 5:10 ~ "6-10 min",
    TRUE ~ NA_character_
  )) %>%
  group_by(cohort,Cohort, ID, phase, Genotype, side_st1, bin) %>%
  summarize(l_dur_5min = sum(Dur_l), r_dur_5min = sum(Dur_r))


# Here the colum $DR_5min is created AND filled in one step. This will raise the warning: Unknown or uninitialised column: `DR_5min`. But it can be ignored.
for (i in 1:nrow(soc_DR2_5min)) {
  if (soc_DR2_5min$side_st1[i] == "r") {
    soc_DR2_5min$DR_5min[i] = (soc_DR2_5min$r_dur_5min[i] - soc_DR2_5min$l_dur_5min[i])/(soc_DR2_5min$r_dur_5min[i] + soc_DR2_5min$l_dur_5min[i])}
  if (soc_DR2_5min$side_st1[i] == "l") {
    soc_DR2_5min$DR_5min[i] = (soc_DR2_5min$l_dur_5min[i] - soc_DR2_5min$r_dur_5min[i])/(soc_DR2_5min$r_dur_5min[i] + soc_DR2_5min$l_dur_5min[i])}
}


rec_DR2_5min <- rec_DR2 %>%
  filter(no!="Sum") %>%
  mutate(bin = case_when(
    no %in% 1:5 ~ "1-5 min",
    no %in% 5:10 ~ "6-10 min",
    TRUE ~ NA_character_
  )) %>%
  group_by(cohort,Cohort, ID, phase, Genotype, side_st1, bin)%>%
  summarize(l_dur_5min = sum(Dur_l), r_dur_5min = sum(Dur_r))
for (i in 1:nrow(rec_DR2_5min)) {
  if (rec_DR2_5min$side_st1[i] == "r") {
    rec_DR2_5min$DR_5min[i] = (rec_DR2_5min$l_dur_5min[i] - rec_DR2_5min$r_dur_5min[i])/(rec_DR2_5min$r_dur_5min[i] + rec_DR2_5min$l_dur_5min[i])}
  if (rec_DR2_5min$side_st1[i] == "l") {
    rec_DR2_5min$DR_5min[i] = (rec_DR2_5min$r_dur_5min[i] - rec_DR2_5min$l_dur_5min[i])/(rec_DR2_5min$r_dur_5min[i] + rec_DR2_5min$l_dur_5min[i])}
}
```

### Results

```{r, echo=FALSE}
# here, a function is created that should perform wilcoxon test to test for significant differences between strains, between strains per cohort and between cohorts per strain. Furthermore, the function creates a table with the columns info, test an sign. The arguments to call the function are DF=data, parameter=variable of interest, info_text=some informational text

make_stats <- function(DF, parameter, info_text) {
  
  #create a tibble called stats
  stats = tibble()
  
  #rename the variable of interest (parameter) with param and save this dataframe into anew variable called stat_data
  stat_data <- DF %>%
  rename(param = parameter)

  # Between strains
  #perform the wilcox_test and tidy the output into a table/tibble
  st = tidy(wilcox.test(param ~ Genotype, stat_data, paired = FALSE)) %>%
    mutate(method = "Wilcoxon rank sum",
         info = info_text,
         test = "between Genotypes for both cohorts",
         sign=ifelse(p.value < 0.05, "*", ""))
  stats = bind_rows(stats, st)

  # Between cohorts
  #st = tidy(wilcox.test(mean_lat ~ cohort, stat_data, paired = TRUE)) %>%
  #  mutate(method = "Wilcoxon",
  #         info = info_text,
  #         test = "between cohorts for both strains",
  #         sign=ifelse(p.value < 0.05, "*", ""))
  #stats = bind_rows(stats, st)


  #between strains per cohort
  #loop over cohorts (hard-coded for 2 cohorts)
  for (k in 1:length(list_of_cohorts)) {
      stat_data_k <- stat_data %>%
        filter(Cohort == k) 
      
      st = tidy(wilcox.test(param ~ Genotype, stat_data_k, paired = FALSE)) %>%
        mutate(method = "Wilcoxon rank sum",
               info = info_text,
               test = paste("between Genotypes for cohort", k),
               sign=ifelse(p.value < 0.05, "*", ""))
      stats = bind_rows(stats, st)
      }
  
  
  #between cohort per strain
  #loop over strains (hard-coded for 2 strains)
  for (k in 1:length(list_of_genotypes)) {
      stat_data_s <- stat_data %>%
        filter(Genotype == list_of_genotypes[k])
      st = tidy(wilcox.test(param ~ Cohort, stat_data_s), paired = TRUE) %>%
        mutate(method = "Wilcoxon signed rank",
               info = info_text,
               test = paste("between cohorts for", list_of_genotypes[k]),
               sign=ifelse(p.value < 0.05, "*", ""))
      stats = bind_rows(stats, st)
}
return(stats)
}
```

```{r PTEN_hab_c1, fig.width = 9, fig.height = 10}
#create a vector with zones and corresponding names to use the zones as labels in the plot
areas <- c("Left", "Center", "Right")
names(areas) <- c("Dur_l", "Dur_c", "Dur_r")

#create a plot object, which does not only contain the plot but also the data and meta-information
PTEN_hab_c1 <- hab %>%
  filter(no=="Sum",
         cohort==1) %>%
  #convert the columns area, strain and cohort into factors with levels corresponding to names(areas), list_of_strains and list_of_cohorts, such that the order will be maintained.
  mutate(area = factor(area, levels = c("Dur_l", "Dur_c", "Dur_r")),
         #Genotype = factor(Genotype, levels = c(list_of_genotypes)),
         Cohort = factor(cohort, levels =c(list_of_cohorts))#,
         #Strain = factor(Strain, levels = c(list_of_strains))
         ) %>%
  #create the plot environment/aesthetics
  ggplot(aes(x = Genotype, y = dur, color = Genotype, label="")) +
  #add a boxplot
  geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NULL) +
  #add color by strain
  scale_colour_manual(values = color_strain) +
  #add ponits shaped by cohort and not overlapping positions
  geom_point(position = position_jitterdodge(dodge.width = 0.05), aes(shape = Cohort), size = 2) +
  #define position of 'n='
  stat_n_text(y.pos = 5) +
  #remove filling (lenght of values needs to be equal to number of cohorts)
  scale_shape_manual(values = c(1,2)) +
  #add a grid/columns by the factors occuring in area and label them according to 'areas'
  facet_grid(.~area, labeller = labeller(area = areas)) +
  #ids as label
  geom_text(hjust = 0, nudge_x = 0.05) +
  #axis title
  labs(x="", 
       y = "Time spent (s)",  
       title = "Habituation phase cohort 1") +
  #add a theme
  theme_pubr() + 
  #legend
  theme(legend.position = "bottom",
        plot.title = element_text(vjust= 0, hjust = 0.5, size = 12))
```

```{r hab_PTEN_stats_c1}

#create a character vector
areas = c("Dur_l", "Dur_c", "Dur_r")

#create a tibble to collect all stats
stats = tibble()

hab_c1 = hab %>% filter(cohort==1)

#iterate for every strain (hard-coded, more general would be: for(i in 1:length(list_of_strain)))
for (i in 1:2) {
  stat_data <- hab_c1 %>%
      filter(no=="Sum", Genotype==list_of_genotypes[i])
  #perform kruskal test duration ~ area
  st = tidy(kruskal.test(stat_data$dur, stat_data$area)) %>%
    #format the output table, add some columns (method,test,info,sign), remove parameter
    mutate(method = "Kruskal",
         test = "habituation",
         info = paste("within for", list_of_genotypes[i]),
         sign=ifelse(p.value < 0.05, "*", "")) %>%
    dplyr::select(-parameter)
  #combine stats from every iteration of the loop
  stats = bind_rows(stats, st)
}

#iterate over areas (hard-coded) and perform wilcox test dur ~ strain
for (i in 1:3){
  stat_data <- hab_c1 %>%
    filter(no=="Sum", area == areas[i])
  st = tidy(wilcox.test(dur ~ Genotype, stat_data, paired = FALSE, conf.int=T)) %>%
    mutate(method = "Wilcoxon rank sum",
         test = "habituation",
         info = paste("b/n genotypes for", if (areas[i]=="Dur_l") {"left"} else if (areas[i]=="Dur_c") {"center"} else "right", "chamber"),
         sign=ifelse(p.value < 0.05, "*", ""))
  stats = bind_rows(stats, st)%>%
    dplyr::select(-alternative)
}

#post-hoc test for strain 1 ( pairwise wilcox test dur ~ area without p-value adjusting)
stat_data <- hab_c1 %>%
  filter(no=="Sum", Genotype == list_of_genotypes[1])
posthoc1_c1 <- pairwise.wilcox.test(stat_data$dur, stat_data$area, p.adjust.method = "none")
posthoc1_c1 <- as_tibble(posthoc1_c1$p.value, rownames = NA)

#post-hoc test for strain 2 ( pairwise wilcox test dur ~ area without p-value adjusting)
stat_data <- hab_c1 %>%
  filter(no=="Sum", Genotype == list_of_genotypes[2])
posthoc2_c1 <- pairwise.wilcox.test(stat_data$dur, stat_data$area, p.adjust.method = "none")
posthoc2_c1 <- as_tibble(posthoc2_c1$p.value, rownames = NA)

#Note: the posthoc test will be displayed at the end of the document

#format the table
stats%>%
  #remove horizontal lines between rows
  kable(booktabs = T) %>%
  #prevent table from floating and scale it to page-width
  kable_styling(latex_options = c("hold_position","scale_down") )

```
From R Documentation: Wilcoxon Rank Sum and Signed Rank Tests: _Note that in the two-sample case the estimator for the difference in location parameters does not estimate the difference in medians (a common misconception) but rather the median of the difference between a sample from x and a sample from y._

```{r stats_PTEN_dur_c1}

#--------------------------STATS FOR DURATION OF INTERACTION ----------------------------#

#copy list of strains as strains
genotypes = list_of_genotypes
#create some character vectors
grids_soc = c("empty", "unfamiliar")
grids_rec = c("familiar", "unfamiliar")

# FOR ZONES
#create a tibble to collect all stats
stats = tibble()

soc_dur_c1 =soc_dur %>% filter(cohort==1)
rec_dur_c1 =rec_dur %>% filter(cohort==1)

#iterate over 2 levels (2 times)
for (i in 1:2) {
  stat_data <- soc_dur_c1 %>%
    #select from vector 'strains' (created above) the index according to number of iteration and filter for that value/string in column strain 
    filter(Genotype == genotypes[i]) 
  #to run a paired test we need the same number of samples with grid = 'empty' as grid = 'unfamiliar'. For animal 62 this data is missing in phase soc.
  #perform wilcoxon signed rank test (paired wilcox test)
  st = tidy(wilcox.test(dur ~ grid, stat_data, paired = TRUE, conf.int=T)) %>%
  # paired because within strain
  mutate(method = "Wilcoxon signed rank",
         test = "social pref by zones",
         info = paste("within", genotypes[i]),
         sign=ifelse(p.value < 0.05, "*", ""))
  stats = bind_rows(stats, st)
  
  stat_data <- soc_dur_c1 %>%
    ##select from vector 'grdi_soc' (created above) the index according to number of iteration and filter for that value/string in column grid
    filter(grid == grids_soc[i])
  #perform wilcox rank sum test (unpaired)
  st = tidy(wilcox.test(dur ~ Genotype, stat_data, paired = FALSE, conf.int=T)) %>%
  # unpaired because between strains
  mutate(method = "Wilcoxon rank sum",
         test = "social pref by zones",
         info = paste("b/n for", grids_soc[i] ),
         sign=ifelse(p.value < 0.05, "*", ""))
  stats = bind_rows(stats, st)
  
  #same as above for rec_dur
  
  stat_data <- rec_dur_c1 %>%
    filter(Genotype == genotypes[i])
  st = tidy(wilcox.test(dur ~ grid, stat_data, paired = TRUE, conf.int=T)) %>%
  # paired because within strain
  mutate(method = "Wilcoxon signed rank",
         test = "social rec by zones",
         info = paste("within", genotypes[i]),
         sign=ifelse(p.value < 0.05, "*", ""))
  stats = bind_rows(stats, st)
  
  stat_data <- rec_dur_c1 %>%
    filter(grid == grids_rec[i])
  st = tidy(wilcox.test(dur ~ Genotype, stat_data, paired = FALSE, conf.int=T)) %>%
  # unpaired because between strains
  mutate(method = "Wilcoxon rank sum",
         test = "social rec by zones",
         info = paste("b/n for", grids_rec[i] ),
         sign=ifelse(p.value < 0.05, "*", ""))
  stats = bind_rows(stats, st)
}

# FOR CHAMBERS
soc_dur2_c1 =soc_dur2 %>% filter(cohort==1)
rec_dur2_c1 =rec_dur2 %>% filter(cohort==1)
stats2 = tibble()
for (i in 1:2) {
```

#### Discrimination ratio or preference for the unfamiliar


__Statistics for Figure 3.__
```{r stats_PTEN_DR_c1}

#--------------------------STATS FOR 10 MIN DR Cohort 1 ----------------------------#

# FOR ZONES
stats = tibble()

stat_data <- soc_DR %>% filter(cohort==1)
st = tidy(wilcox.test(DR ~ Genotype, stat_data, paired = FALSE, conf.int=T)) %>%
# unpaired because between strains
  mutate(method = "Wilcoxon rank sum",
       test = "social pref by zones",
       info = "b/n genotypes",
       sign=ifelse(p.value < 0.05, "*", ""))
stats = bind_rows(stats, st)


stat_data <- rec_DR %>% filter(cohort==1)
st = tidy(wilcox.test(DR ~ Genotype, stat_data, paired = FALSE, conf.int=T)) %>%
# unpaired because between strains
  mutate(method = "Wilcoxon rank sum",
       test = "social rec by zones",
       info = paste("b/n genotypes"),
       sign=ifelse(p.value < 0.05, "*", ""))
stats = bind_rows(stats, st)

#iterate over strain and test against theoretical mean of 0
for (i in 1:2){
  stat_data <- soc_DR %>%
    filter(cohort==1) %>% 
    filter(Genotype==genotypes[i])
  st = tidy(wilcox.test(stat_data$DR, mu = 0, conf.int=T)) %>%
    mutate(method = "Wilcoxon rank sum",
           test = "social pref by zones",
           info = paste("compared to 0 for", genotypes[i]),
           sign=ifelse(p.value < 0.05, "*", ""))
  stats = bind_rows(stats, st)

  stat_data <- rec_DR %>%
    filter(cohort==1) %>%
    filter(Genotype==genotypes[i])
  st = tidy(wilcox.test(stat_data$DR, mu = 0, conf.int=T)) %>%
    mutate(method = "Wilcoxon signed rank",
           test = "social rec by zones",
           info = paste("compared to 0 for", genotypes[i]),
           sign=ifelse(p.value < 0.05, "*", ""))
  stats = bind_rows(stats, st)
}


# FOR CHAMBERS
stats2 = tibble()
stat_data <- soc_DR2 %>% filter(cohort==1)
st = tidy(wilcox.test(DR ~ Genotype, stat_data, paired = FALSE, conf.int=T)) %>%
# unpaired because between strains
  mutate(method = "Wilcoxon rank sum",
       test = "social pref by chambers",
       info = paste("b/n genotypes"),
       sign=ifelse(p.value < 0.05, "*", ""))
stats2 = bind_rows(stats2, st)

stat_data <- rec_DR2 %>% filter(cohort==1) 
st = tidy(wilcox.test(DR ~ Genotype, stat_data, paired = FALSE, conf.int=T)) %>%
# unpaired because between strains
  mutate(method = "Wilcoxon rank sum",
       test = "social rec by chambers",
       info = paste("b/n genotypes"),
       sign=ifelse(p.value < 0.05, "*", ""))
stats2 = bind_rows(stats2, st)

#iterate over strain and test against theoretical mean of 0
for (i in 1:2){
  stat_data <- soc_DR2 %>%
    filter(cohort==1) %>%
    filter(Genotype==genotypes[i])
  st = tidy(wilcox.test(stat_data$DR, mu = 0, conf.int=T)) %>%
    mutate(method = "Wilcoxon signed rank",
           test = "social pref by chambers",
           info = paste("compared to 0 for", genotypes[i]),
           sign=ifelse(p.value < 0.05, "*", ""))
  stats2 = bind_rows(stats2, st)

  stat_data <- rec_DR2 %>%
    filter(cohort==1) %>%
    filter(Genotype==genotypes[i])
  st = tidy(wilcox.test(stat_data$DR, mu = 0, conf.int=T)) %>%
    mutate(method = "Wilcoxon signed rank",
           test = "social rec by chambers",
           info = paste("compared to 0 for", genotypes[i]),
           sign=ifelse(p.value < 0.05, "*", ""))
  stats2 = bind_rows(stats2, st)
}

scharff_statDR <- bind_rows(stats, stats2)%>%
  dplyr::select(-alternative)
scharff_statDR %>%
  kable(booktabs = T) %>%
  kable_styling(latex_options = c("hold_position","scale_down") )

```
From R Documentation: Wilcoxon Rank Sum and Signed Rank Tests: _Note that in the two-sample case the estimator for the difference in location parameters does not estimate the difference in medians (a common misconception) but rather the median of the difference between a sample from x and a sample from y._

__Figure 4.__ Cohort 1: Discrimination ratio shown by 5-minute bins during the social preference (A) and social recognition (B) test phases. The dashed line represents chance level.

__Statistics for Figure 4.__

```{r stats_PTEN_DR5min_c1}

#--------------------------STATS FOR 5 MIN BIN DR Cohort 1 ----------------------------#

bins <- c("1-5 min", "6-10 min")

# FOR CHAMBERS ONLY
stats = tibble()
#iterate over strains and test for difference between bins within each strain
for (i in 1:2) {
  stat_data <- soc_DR2_5min %>%
    filter(cohort==1) %>% 
    filter(Genotype == genotypes[i])
  st = tidy(wilcox.test(DR_5min ~ bin, stat_data, paired = TRUE, conf.int=T)) %>%
  # paired because within strain
  mutate(method = "Wilcoxon signed rank",
         test = "social pref by chambers",
         info = paste("within", genotypes[i]),
         sign=ifelse(p.value < 0.05, "*", ""))
  stats = bind_rows(stats, st)
  
  #iterate over bins and test for difference between strains within each bin
  stat_data <- soc_DR2_5min %>%
    filter(cohort==1) %>% 
    filter(bin == bins[i])
  st = tidy(wilcox.test(DR_5min ~ Genotype, stat_data, paired = FALSE, conf.int=T)) %>%
  # unpaired because between strains
  mutate(method = "Wilcoxon rank sum",
         test = "social pref by chambers",
         info = paste("b/n for", bins[i]),
         sign=ifelse(p.value < 0.05, "*", ""))
  stats = bind_rows(stats, st)
  
  #use index i from outer loop above to iterate over bins and inner loop to iterate over strains.
  # Test for a difference to a theoretical mean of 0 for each strain in each 5 min bin
  for (k in 1:2) {
    stat_data <- soc_DR2_5min %>%
      filter(cohort==1) %>% 
      filter(bin==bins[i], Genotype==genotypes[k])
    st = tidy(wilcox.test(stat_data$DR_5min, mu = 0, conf.int=T)) %>%
      mutate(method = "Wilcoxon signed rank",
             test = "social pref by chambers",
             info = paste("compared to 0 for", genotypes[k], bins[i]),
             sign=ifelse(p.value < 0.05, "*", ""))
    stats = bind_rows(stats, st)
    }

  #Same as above but for rec_DR2_5min
  
  stat_data <- rec_DR2_5min %>%
    filter(cohort==1) %>% 
    filter(Genotype == genotypes[i])
  st = tidy(wilcox.test(DR_5min ~ bin, stat_data, paired = TRUE, conf.int=T)) %>%
  # paired because within strain
  mutate(method = "Wilcoxon signed rank",
         test = "social rec by chambers",
         info = paste("within", genotypes[i]),
         sign=ifelse(p.value < 0.05, "*", ""))
  stats = bind_rows(stats, st)
  
  stat_data <- rec_DR2_5min %>%
    filter(cohort==1) %>% 
    filter(bin == bins[i])
  st = tidy(wilcox.test(DR_5min ~ Genotype, stat_data, paired = FALSE, conf.int=T)) %>%
  mutate(method = "Wilcoxon rank sum",
         test = "social rec by chambers",
         info = paste("b/n for", bins[i] ),
         sign=ifelse(p.value < 0.05, "*", ""))
  stats = bind_rows(stats, st)

 for (k in 1:2) {
    stat_data <- rec_DR2_5min %>%
      filter(cohort==1) %>% 
      filter(bin==bins[i], Genotype==genotypes[k])
    st = tidy(wilcox.test(stat_data$DR_5min, mu = 0, conf.int=T)) %>%
      mutate(method = "Wilcoxon signed rank",
             test = "social rec by chambers",
             info = paste("compared to 0 for", genotypes[k], bins[i]),
             sign=ifelse(p.value < 0.05, "*", ""))
    stats = bind_rows(stats, st)
    }

}


PTEN_statDR2_5min_c1<- stats %>%
  dplyr::select(-alternative)
PTEN_statDR2_5min_c1 %>%
  kable(booktabs = T) %>%
  kable_styling(latex_options = c("hold_position","scale_down") )
```
